newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil restricts overseas credit card purchases.
newsitem.headline: Brazil restricts overseas credit card purchases.

text.p: Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) Thursday restricted credit card purchases abroad by prohibiting them to be financed, Central Bank Director of Controls Alkimar Moura said.
Moura told reporters goods and services bought overseas by Brazilians using credit cards would have to be paid in cash once the credit card bill came due and could not be paid in installments.
Moura declined to comment on the possible effect of the new regulation, which will be published Friday in the government's Official Journal.
Faced with a mounting trade deficit, the government recently increased the tax on credit operations to curb consumption of imported household appliances and restricted short-term import financing.
The trade deficit in the first four months of 1997 totalled about $4.0 billion. So far in May, the country is running a $24 million deficit.
